title: Integration and System Testing
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its role in reliable software.
Identify the topic in code or a realistic scenario.
Trace behavior and describe the expected result.
Apply the concept and verify it using a suitable test.

understand.concept: Integration testing checks how components work together—for example, a function with a data layer or a form with validation and submission. System testing evaluates the assembled application against end-to-end requirements in an environment resembling its intended use. Scope and tooling vary by project.
understand.whyItMatters: Components can pass isolated tests but fail at interfaces, configuration, data formats, timing, or environment assumptions.
understand.analogy: Investigating a problem or checking a process uses observations, clear expectations, and controlled steps rather than guesswork.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is a simplification; software behavior depends on runtime, interfaces, and the specific system.

explain.narrative: Identify the components and interface contracts. Verify that data shapes, error paths, sequencing, and configuration agree. Then test representative complete workflows from user action through the resulting state or output. Keep environment-specific assumptions documented.

examples.title: Compatible interface
examples.explanation: The component expects an object with a name string; integration must provide that shape.

examples.title: End-to-end sequence
examples.explanation: A system-level test follows the workflow through connected steps.

examples.title: Contract mismatch
examples.explanation: A component may expect a number but receive a string from another component.

examples.title: Mock boundary
examples.explanation: A controlled substitute can isolate an integration boundary during testing.

examples.title: Check full result
examples.explanation: A workflow test checks the resulting state and user feedback, not only that a function ran.

commonMistakes: Testing a workflow in an unrealistic environment.
Treating a mock as proof that the real service works.
Checking only that a click or request occurred.
